model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on tangible book (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock (Series D, G/L, I, J, K etc., carrying value)
equity_bridge.note: Senior to common; deducted at carrying value at 2026-06-30 rather than charging the ~$232M/yr preferred dividend to the flows (the more conservative of the two at a 10.25% cost of equity: 232 / 0.1025 = 2,263 < 3,559). Derived from the equity section of the 10-Q balance sheet (XBRL carries no PreferredStockValue tag since 2013). August 2026 Series L issue assumed to refinance the $750M Series G one-for-one.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2031 average revenue growth (4.5-5.0%); equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because STT returns ~80% of earnings and swapped $1.5B of preferred out in FY2024, which mechanically suppresses book growth without describing earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 1.2% vs revenue 3.6% and EPS 8.3% - divergence >30%. Cause is distribution policy (diluted share count cut from 357.1M FY2020 to 289.0M FY2025, -19%) and AOCI swings, not a deteriorating franchise. EPS CAGRs are buyback-flattered: net income grew only 4.0%/yr over the same five years.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are computed on NET INCOME (the FCFE proxy: FY2025 2,945 vs FY2022 2,774 vs FY2020 2,420), not on the CSV's reported FCF, which is deposit-flow noise for a custody bank (FY2024 -14,136, FY2025 +10,843). Revenue: FY2025 13,944 / FY2022 12,148 / FY2020 11,703. EPS (CSV, basic): 9.55 / 7.28 / 6.40. Equity (total, incl. preferred): 27,841 / 25,191 / 26,200. FY2025 net income is depressed by $326M restructuring; ex that, the 5-yr NI CAGR is ~5.5%. FY2026E is a step-change year (+13% revenue, record markets) that the CAGRs do not yet contain.

scenario_narratives.base: State Street's value turns on four axes: (1) servicing-fee growth on a record $57.9T of AUC/A, which the base case holds at mid-single digits as ~$384B/quarter of new mandates onboard and markets compound, against persistent custody fee compression; (2) SSGA/SPDR management fees on $6.3T AUM, which ride ETF adoption but are market-level sensitive; (3) net interest income (~21% of revenue), which gives back part of 2026's +14-15% as the Fed eases; and (4) operating leverage from the $1B transformation programme, which lifts the pretax margin from FY2026's ~32% to 33.5% - most of management's ~35% medium-term target, discounted for STT's history of never sustaining much above 30%. Revenue grows 4.5-5% to FY2031 and 3% thereafter; FY2027 is modelled soft (+4.5%, 50bps margin give-back) because 2026 was lifted by record markets and trading volumes management itself does not extrapolate. ~85% of earnings is distributed through the $0.92 quarterly dividend and buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Equity markets keep compounding and the mandate pipeline converts: fee revenue grows high-single-digit for two more years, State Street Alpha and the Latam securities-services acquisition add genuine new revenue lines, and the 2026 operating-leverage run-rate persists so the 35% pretax target is hit by FY2029 and slightly exceeded. Capital-light fee growth (0.7x retention) lets payout stay ~85-90%. Digital-asset/tokenisation custody optionality is NOT separately priced - it is upside to this case, not inside it.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 peak reverses in FY2027: a 15-20% equity correction cuts AUC/A- and AUM-linked fees with a one-to-two-quarter lag, FX and securities-finance volumes fall from records, and Fed easing compresses NII, so revenue falls 3% against a sticky cost base and the pretax margin drops back to ~28%. Fee compression then holds growth to 2.5-3%, the transformation programme stalls at a 30% margin, the balance sheet consumes capital faster than revenue (1.1x retention, G-SIB surcharge creep), and the market exits at 12x FCFE. No solvency element - this is an earnings reset and de-rating, not a credit event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: State Street is a fee-led custody bank and asset manager that distributes ~80% of its earnings, so it is valued as a stream of free cash flow to equity (net income less the common equity retained to grow the balance sheet at a G-SIB CET1 level) capitalised at a 10.25% USD cost of equity, with deposits and wholesale funding treated as operating liabilities and only the ~$3.56B of preferred stock deducted ahead of common. FY0 is the FY2026 guided run-rate (revenue +13%, ~32% pretax margin) ex the Q1 restructuring charge, and the record Q2 is not annualised. The three cases differ on whether 2026's market-driven revenue step holds, how much of the 35% pretax-margin target the transformation programme delivers, and how much capital balance-sheet growth absorbs.
key_risks_to_valuation: Market levels: ~60% of revenue (servicing and management fees) is ad-valorem on AUC/A and AUM; a 20% equity drawdown cuts fee revenue high-single-digits with a lag - the bear case's FY2027 -3%

Net interest income (~21% of revenue) is the second swing factor: FY2026's +14-15% NII growth reverses if the Fed eases faster than the forward curve, and deposits ($319.5B, up $45B in H1-2026) can leave as fast as they arrived
Margin execution: the base case takes the pretax margin to 33.5%, a level STT has not sustained; each 1pp of terminal pretax margin is worth roughly $6/share
Capital: as a G-SIB, CET1 requirements, the G-SIB surcharge and any Basel III endgame re-proposal set the retention the model charges; the bear case lifts retention to 1.1x growth
Unmodelled: the pending Santander/CACEIS Latam acquisition (undisclosed terms, 2027 close) and the August 2026 Series L preferred / Series G refinancing (assumed one-for-one)

The model holds the share count flat and treats buybacks as the FCFE distribution channel; per-share value is insensitive to repurchase pace but sensitive to the 10.25% cost of equity and the 21.5% tax rate (see sensitivity grid)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 104.64-195.93
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000093751): FY2025 10-K filed 2026-02-19 and Q2-2026 10-Q filed 2026-07-30 for revenues, NII, noninterest income/expense, pretax income, tax, preferred dividends, buybacks, dividends, capex, goodwill, intangibles, equity components, AOCI, deposits and share counts; EDGAR full-text search for the August 2026 preferred filings (documents themselves returned HTTP 403); STT_Metrics.csv (XBRL-derived) for the FY2007-FY2025 history
data_sources.qualitative: STT_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q2-2026 results and raised FY2026 guidance (fee revenue +12-13%, NII +14-15%, ~500bps operating leverage), medium-term ~35% pretax margin and mid-20s ROTCE targets, $1B transformation programme, Latam acquisition, dividend increase to $0.92

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E total revenue (fee revenue + NII + other income), built from H1-2026 actuals (Revenues 7,844 = NII 1,695 + noninterest income 6,148) and management's twice-raised Q2-2026 guidance: fee revenue +12-13% on FY2025's ~10,744 (=> ~12,090) plus other income ~300, NII +14-15% on FY2025's 2,960 (=> ~3,390). Total ~15,750, +13.0% on FY2025's 13,944; H2 implied 7,906 vs a Q2 run-rate of 8,096, so the anchor does not annualise the record Q2. No revenue notables identified in 2026 (realised AFS gains/losses ~0 every quarter).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 10-Q cover-page common shares outstanding 274,701,765 at 2026-07-28 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, filed 2026-07-30) plus 4.9M dilutive awards (Q2-2026 diluted weighted average 281.062M less basic 276.150M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed inside noninterest expense (and therefore inside the pretax margin); buybacks ($1,200M FY2025, $800M H1-2026, ~$400M/quarter run-rate) are the FCFE distribution channel, not a modelled count reduction. Q3-2026 repurchases (~2.3M shares at ~$170 if the $400M pace held) are not yet filed and are deliberately not anticipated.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank convention (house precedent NTRS, NAB.AX, HBAN, GL): deposits ($319.5B at 2026-06-30), short-term borrowings and senior/subordinated long-term debt are operating funding of a deposit-taking custodian, serviced inside net interest income (FY2025 interest expense on long-term debt $1,230M is already netted in NII). FCFE is post-interest, so net debt is held at 0 and the flows are capitalised at the cost of equity. The only claim senior to common deducted is preferred stock (equity_bridge). Cash & due from banks ($4.29B) and interest-bearing deposits at banks ($145.2B) are operating assets funding client deposits, not surplus cash.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: net income ex-notables ~3,956 (pretax 5,040 = 32.0% of 15,750, at a 21.5% tax rate) x the ~75% payout actually realised in H1-2026 (buybacks 800 + common dividends 464 + preferred dividends 116 = 1,380 vs net income 1,848). reported_fcf is the CSV's FY2025 OCF-less-capex (11,898 - 1,055 = 10,843) and is deposit/trading-asset flow noise for a custody bank (FY2024 was -14,136, H1-2026 -15,414 on the same business); recorded for auditability only. The owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: ESTIMATE. STT stopped tagging AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense in XBRL after FY2018 ($262M FY2018, $243-355M FY2013-18, 2.1-3.6% of revenue); the FY2025 10-K/Q2-2026 10-Q text could not be retrieved this session (SEC Archives returned HTTP 403; only the companyfacts API and full-text search responded). FY2025 carries a tagged $79M of accelerated compensation cost. ~2.0% of revenue (~$280M) is assumed. It sits INSIDE noninterest expense, so it does not move the house value; sbc_pct_path is carried only so the engine's house/street memo band is computed. Refresh from the FY2026 10-K equity-compensation note.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS part of the business for a custody bank (NII 2,960 FY2025, ~21% of revenue). No cash is added back to value, so there is no double count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,200M + common dividends $909M + preferred dividends $226M = $2,335M returned vs $2,945M net income (79% total payout; management's medium-term target is ~80%). H1-2026: buybacks $800M + common dividends $464M + preferred $116M. Quarterly dividend $0.84, planned +10% to $0.92 from Q3-2026 ($3.68 annualised, 2.1% yield at the current price).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the FY2026 guided ex-notables estimate (fiscal year closes 31 Dec 2026, nine months elapsed at the valuation date), so Y1 = FY2027. Last fully reported year is FY2025; latest filing is the Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-30). Q3-2026 results are due mid-October 2026 and should trigger a refresh.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-07-28 (10-Q cover page); dilution from Q2-2026 weighted averages

balance_sheet_anchors.preferred_note: Preferred carrying value is not tagged in XBRL; derived as total equity 28,268 less common 504, APIC 10,710, retained earnings 32,660, AOCI -1,178 and treasury -17,987 = 3,559 (identical 3,559 at 2025-12-31). Annual preferred dividends ~$232M (6.5% on carrying value). EDGAR full-text search shows a new Series L preferred issued 2026-08-05/07 (424B5, 8-K items 3.03/5.03) and a 2026-07-23 8-K referencing Series G and $750,000,000, consistent with a refinancing of the $750M Series G; the documents themselves returned HTTP 403, so the post-August preferred stack is treated as unchanged at 3,559 and should be confirmed at the Q3-2026 10-Q.
balance_sheet_anchors.roatce_fy0_est: FY2026E net income to common ~3,725 / TCE 15,787 = ~23.6%, against a medium-term target of 'mid-20s'

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.25% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.2. Higher than NTRS's 9.75% (beta 1.1) because STT carries more market-sensitive revenue: SSGA management fees on $6.3T AUM, FX trading and securities finance (~13% of revenue) and a 52-week range of 104.64-195.93 that shows equity-like beta. Single rate across all three scenarios so risk is charged once, through the probability weights. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine's field name; no debt is in the capital structure being discounted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (premises, including the One Congress Boston HQ) are expensed inside noninterest expense (occupancy 487 FY2025) and therefore inside the pretax margin; no lease liability is added to net debt (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income is fully attributable to the parent.
inputs.engine_mapping: The component engine is driven as a bank P&L: 'EBITDA margin' = pretax-income margin + D&A % (7.0) + SBC % (2.0), so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = pretax income; cash_tax_rate 21.5% (FY2025 effective 21.1%, H1-2026 21.6%; FY2025 cash taxes paid 594 vs 786 book) turns that into net income before preferred dividends. da_pct and capex_pct share a 7.0% core (FY2025 capex 1,055 = 7.6% of revenue; depreciation is no longer tagged in XBRL - only the DIFFERENCE between the two paths matters on this route, plus the tax shield which nets to zero because D&A is inside EBITDA). The EXCESS of capex_pct over da_pct is the common equity retained to grow the balance sheet and RWA: retention = k x revenue growth, k = 0.8 base / 0.7 bull / 1.1 bear (TCE/revenue is ~1.0x; over FY2020-25 total equity grew 1.2%/yr while revenue grew 3.6%/yr on a ~80-110% payout, so most of STT's growth is ad-valorem fee growth on AUC/A that consumes little capital). Working-capital capture is 0. FCFE = net income - retained capital, capitalised at the cost of equity; preferred is deducted at carrying value in the bridge instead of its ~$232M dividend being charged to the flows. Acquired-intangible amortisation (223 FY2025, running off) is left inside the pretax margin uncredited - a deliberate conservatism worth ~$0.60/share/yr.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity, through the component engine route - the routing table's bank row (residual income on tangible book) implemented as the house precedent for custody/trust banks (NTRS 2026-10-02) and NAB.AX/HBAN/GL: net_debt = 0, preferred deducted in equity_bridge, retention tied to growth. BVPS-compounding rejected because STT distributes ~80% of earnings and book has compounded 1.2%/yr (FY2020-25) while EPS compounded 8.3% - book is not the value driver, distributable earnings are. Owner-FCF DCF rejected because OCF swings from -13,210 (FY2024) to +11,898 (FY2025) on deposit and trading-asset flows. SBC: expensed (inside noninterest expense), share count held flat, funded by a real buyback programme. FY0 ANCHOR: FY2026E ex-notables (revenue 15,750, pretax margin 32.0% per guidance of ~500bps operating leverage, net income ~3,956, net to common ~3,725, EPS ~$13.3 on 279.6M diluted shares - 13.1x at the current price). Notables: Q1-2026 restructuring $89M (excluded from the FY0 margin); no Q2-2026 notable tagged. The record Q2-2026 (34.3% pretax margin, EPS $3.65) is NOT annualised. NOT MODELLED: the pending Santander/CACEIS Latam securities-services acquisition (terms undisclosed, close 2027) - it is neither in the flows nor the bridge. DATA FLAGS for the parent: (1) SBC is an estimate (see sbc_source); (2) preferred stock carrying value is derived, and the August 2026 Series L issue / Series G redemption is inferred from EDGAR full-text-search hits, not read; (3) SEC Archives (www.sec.gov/Archives) returned HTTP 403 for every document this session - only data.sec.gov companyfacts and efts full-text search worked; (4) CSV EPS is basic (FY2025 9.55 vs diluted 9.40).

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [28.0, 28.0, 28.5, 29.0, 29.5, 30.0, ...]: FY2027 revenue falls 3% (a 15-20% equity-market correction cuts ad-valorem servicing and SSGA fees, FX/securities-finance volumes fall from 2026 records, Fed easing compresses NII from the 1.13% Q2-26 NIM) against a sticky cost base, so the margin returns to FY2025's ex-notables ~28-29% and the transformation programme only reaches 30%.
bear.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 1.1 x revenue growth (balance sheet and RWA grow faster than revenue), floored at zero in FY2027 when revenue shrinks (no capital release assumed); terminal cap 12x FCFE reflects a de-rated custodian growing 2.5%.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin = EBITDA - SBC - D&A = [31.5, 32.5, 33.0, 33.5, 33.5, ...]: FY2027 gives back 50bps from FY0's 32.0% as FX/securities-finance activity and NII normalise off the 2026 peak, then the $1B transformation programme lifts it to 33.5% by FY2030 - most, not all, of management's ~35% medium-term target (STT has never sustained above ~30% reported).
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.8 x revenue growth = [3.6, 4.0, 4.0, 3.6, 3.6, 3.2, 3.2, 2.8, 2.4, 2.4]% of revenue, i.e. ~14-15% of net income in FY2027-28 (an ~85% payout, near management's ~80% target) falling to ~9% at the 3% terminal growth rate.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.25%/3.0% is 14.2x FCFE, under the 15x cap, so Gordon binds. 15x FCFE (~13.6x net income) is at the upper end of where custody banks have historically traded on earnings; the base IV implies ~14x FY2027E EPS.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [33.0, 34.0, 35.0, 35.5, 35.5, ...]: the transformation programme delivers its full $1B run-rate by 2029, management's ~35% pretax target is hit on time and slightly exceeded.
bull.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.7 x revenue growth: Alpha software, ETF management fees and mandate wins are capital-light, so less CET1 is consumed per dollar of revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25, matching the custody-bank precedent (NTRS). Bear raised to 25% because the Analysis rates an equity/bond market correction as the single high-severity risk, FY2026 earnings are visibly lifted by record market levels and trading volumes, and the stock trades near the top of its 52-week range after a ~65% rise off the low. Bull cut to 25% because it needs the $1B transformation programme to fully land, markets to keep rising and NII to hold, all at once, and STT's record of hitting margin targets is mixed. Base at 50% is the guided path with partial credit for the medium-term targets.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
